recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. If the work group later wants required standard codes or a stronger binding, that should be handled by a new tracker; FHIR-46494's applied documentation/example request is already represented in active core source.
issue_request: FHIR-46494 was Applied/Persuasive for FHIR-core R6 and requested documentation and examples showing how authorization information can be included in subscription notifications, based on the Backport IG authorization-hint work in FHIR-43081 and incorporating FHIR-44102 wording clarification.
initial_application: The source change was already present before this reconciliation. Commit 0857a9913b, merged through HL7/fhir#3967, added SubscriptionStatus.notificationEvent.authorizationHint, an id-only notification example with authorizationHint, and an Authorization Hinting in Notifications subsection. Later commit e47a0d9002 refined the authorizationType/value labels and definitions.
additional_context: FHIR-43081 approved the backport authorization-hint concept as coded type plus optional value for notification events, and FHIR-44102 clarified that the type conveys how the sibling value is used. FHIR-I minutes show the backport-to-R6 batch was queued on 2024-07-29 and FHIR-46494 was approved 11-0-0 on 2024-08-05. source/fhir.ini actively includes SubscriptionStatus, so the checked StructureDefinition and examples are in build scope.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source already contains SubscriptionStatus.notificationEvent.authorizationHint with authorizationType Coding and optional value, an id-only notification example using authorizationHint, and narrative guidance about secure authorization information, including short-lived and single-use tokens. The current authorizationType/value wording sufficiently carries the FHIR-44102 clarification.
source_changes: No source files were changed by this reconciliation; the published commit is an empty audit commit.
